1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version

18

21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run

I couldn't pin down exactly what filled the context, because I can't see the session that failed. Here is what the code does show, and what I'd change.

**Prelude's starting payload isn't the 1.2M.** At the start of a turn, Prelude sends three things:
- The design prompt (`designPrompt` in `server/agent.js:293`), which is a few thousand tokens.
- Five tools (`TOOLS` in `server/agent.js:32`).
- Your message (`promptOf` in `server/main.js:2779`), plus any findings from the last check (`withFindings`, `server/turns.js:68`).

None of that comes close to 1.2M tokens.

**The error comes from Claude Code, and the count built up during the agent's first turn.** "A single-exchange conversation cannot be compacted" means only one message from you had been sent. Everything after it was the agent's own tool calls and results, plus the files and images Claude Code attached along the way. Claude Code normally compacts the conversation before it gets that full. It can't compact the first exchange, though, so one long first turn has no way out. That happens if the agent reads a lot: big states JSON, screenshots, or reference folders such as OrchestratR (passed with `--add-dir`, `server/agent.js:76`).

**The failed session is now stuck.** Once the CLI starts, Prelude marks the session `started: true` (`server/turns.js:227`). Your next message in that session runs with `--resume` against the same oversized conversation, and should fail the same way. The only failure Prelude recovers from is "no conversation found" (`server/agent.js:124`), which starts afresh with a recap (`server/turns.js:264`). "Prompt is too long" falls through as a plain error.

**What you can do now:** start a new session on that design, and keep the first message narrower so the agent's first turn reads less.

**To find the actual cause:** the session ran in the design's worktree under `~/.prelude/worktrees/…`, which I can't read from here. If you tell me which design it was, or attach that session's `transcript.jsonl`, I can see which reads blew it up.

**What I'd change, on a branch:**
- **`server/agent.js`** (`createCliRunner`): recognise a result saying "Prompt is too long" and return `{ lost: true }` with a friendly message. The session would then restart once from its recap and the design's files, instead of failing on every resume.
- **`server/turns.js`** (`withFindings`): cap how many findings are sent, and how long each one can be, as the `differ` list already does at line 316. This one is defensive: the findings are the only part of the first message with no upper bound.
- **`server/agent.js`** (`designPrompt`): add a line asking the agent to read only what the request needs, and to read reference folders selectively.

It looks like a lot of sessions were created at the same time

Those sessions weren't all created at 12:01. Each folder's name starts with the date it was made (`20261018-0730-…` was made on 18 October at 07:30), so they date from 18 to 22 October.

What they share is **LastWriteTime**. On Windows, a folder's LastWriteTime changes whenever a file is added inside it. Design sessions run in the design's worktree, and a design gets its worktree the first time something is posted on its page ("anything posted makes the branch first", `CLAUDE.md`, Branches; `server/branches.js:431`). Creating the worktree checks out every committed session folder at once, so they all show the moment of the checkout. Updating the branch from main would do the same. So the worktree was probably made or updated at 12:01, and all twelve folders show that time. Nothing in the listing points to sessions being created twice.

The one that matters is the last folder, **`20261023-1203-lx77`**. It's the only one made today, at 12:03, which fits you starting a session just after the worktree appeared. That should be the session that failed. Its files are:

- `…\sessions\20261023-1203-lx77\transcript.jsonl` (Prelude's record)
- `…\sessions\20261023-1203-lx77\session.json`, which holds the `claudeSessionId` for Claude Code's full copy under `~\.claude\projects\…`

text:
Found it. Prelude itself sent the huge message, and there's a real fault on the branch behind it.

**What happened**

1. **A view on the branch has merge conflict markers in it.** The text that was sent includes `<<<<<<< HEAD` inside the header comment of `server/views/projects/_app.eta`. That comment ("The app (step 8): its stack…") exists only in `_app.eta` and `_folder.eta`. Main's copy of `server/views/` has no markers, so they exist only in the branch's worktree. My guess is they came from bringing main into the branch around 12:01, the time on all those session folders, but I can't confirm it from here. With both sides of the conflict left in, the template declares `p` twice. Eta refuses to compile it: "Bad template syntax: Identifier 'p' has already been declared".

2. **Prelude's check reports that error many times over, each copy huge.** Project Landing Page's routes use the app's own views (`prelude/project-landing-page/routes.json`). The project page renders `_app.eta`, so after the last turn every route that renders it failed, in every state. Eta's message for a syntax error includes the whole compiled template, tens of KB of generated code. One copy of that is recorded per route per state.

3. **All of those copies went in front of your message.** `withFindings` (`server/turns.js:68`) adds every finding to the start of the next message, whatever its number or size. That made your one-line request about 8 MB (the `.jsonl` you measured). The "conversation" half of the error is that message. I can't account for the other ~545k exactly, but it's clearly the same blow-up, not anything Claude Code added. The only attachment shown is the small environment note.

**What to do now**

Start a new session on Project Landing Page and ask it first to resolve the conflict markers in `server/views/projects/_app.eta`, keeping both sides' changes. The oversized findings were cleared when the failed turn started (`findings.delete`, `server/turns.js:259`), so a new session won't carry them. 1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

4	short: Prompts and the Claude CLI
5	files: server/agent.js
6	uses: stories, visuals, claude
7	
8	Runs the Claude Code CLI and holds every prompt Prelude gives it: design, build, app build, connect, story, fix and ask. It also holds the architecture briefs: one for changing code, and a read-only one for ask. Once the project has an architecture, every prompt gets the visual vocabulary, taken from `visuals`. It sets the permission flags that fence what the agent may read and write, and normalises the CLI's stream into transcript entries.
9	
10	## Responsible for
11	- The prompt for each kind of design and each mode
12	- The architecture briefs, and the vocabulary in design, build, fix and ask prompts
13	- `--allowedTools` and `--add-dir`: never a bare Read, Glob or Grep
14	- Spawning and resuming the CLI, and summarising its tool calls
15	
16	## Not its job
17	- When a turn runs, or what's done with its output (turns)
18	- Choosing which Koda the prompts point at (designs, server)
19	- Describing the vocabulary: visuals does, so the parser and its description change together
20	
21	## Owns
22	- The prompts and permission rules

I've made the four changes on this branch. I couldn't run the tests here, so please run `npm test`, especially `test/host.test.js`, `test/chat.test.js` and `test/build.test.js`.

**What caused it:** `server/views/projects/_app.eta` on `prelude/project-landing-page` had git conflict markers committed in it, so the view wouldn't compile. Every route and state that renders that view failed. Each failure carried Eta's error, which includes the whole compiled template. All of them went in front of your one-line message, which made it about 8 MB. The CLI then refused it as too long, and treated that as an ordinary error, so the session stayed stuck.

**What changed:**
- **Findings are short now** (`server/turns.js`, `withFindings`). The same error is reported once, naming up to 6 places where it happened plus "and N more". Each error is cut to 20 lines or 1,500 characters, and each kind lists at most 20 different problems.
- **Eta errors are readable** (`server/renderer.js`). A view that won't compile now reports Eta's message without the compiled code, and names the view's file.
- **A conversation that's too long starts afresh** (`server/agent.js`, `server/main.js`). "Prompt is too long" is now handled like a conversation that can't be resumed. The session restarts once with a new conversation, told what was said so far, instead of failing on every message. Every session now gets that summary, not just ones moved onto a fix's branch. So a session that "can't be resumed on this machine" now restarts by itself too, instead of asking you to start a new one.
- **Conflict markers can't be committed during an update from main** (`server/branches.js`, `merging`). Before, Prelude only checked the files it had recorded as clashing. Now it also checks every file git still lists as unmerged.

**Two limits:**
- I can't confirm the markers got in through that gap in `branches.js`; it's the most likely route I found.
- Markers committed some other way are still only caught when they break a page the after-turn check renders, as happened here.

**Tests added:**
- A view that won't compile reports a short error naming its file (`host.test.js`).
- 80 copies of one huge failure are reported as one short line (`host.test.js`).
- "Prompt is too long" counts as a lost conversation (`chat.test.js`).
- A design session whose conversation is lost restarts once, told what was said (`chat.test.js`).
- An unmerged clash Prelude has no record of still blocks the commit (`build.test.js`).

No designs changed and the architecture is unaffected; I didn't propose a decision. The notes for you to check are in `prelude/fixes/i-just-got-this-error-trying-to-start-a-design-session/NOTES.md`.
